name: Esquimalt

facts.text: Esquimalt's Tree Protection Bylaw, 2022, No. 3076 protects trees by species and any tree over 30 cm in diameter, measured at breast height (1.4 m).
facts.sourceTitle: Esquimalt Tree Cutting Permit | Township of Esquimalt
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); the species list was cut off in the snippet

facts.text: In Esquimalt a tree permit covers removal, pruning, or work in a protected tree's root zone. Applications go to trees@esquimalt.ca, and on building projects the tree permit is handled with the building permit.
facts.sourceTitle: Esquimalt Tree Cutting Permit | Township of Esquimalt
facts.excerpt: removal, pruning, or work in the protected root zone
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Esquimalt's Natural Environment Development Permit Area (DPA 1) covers new buildings, additions over 10 m² and landscaping, with some exceptions. Township-approved ecological restoration is exempt.
facts.excerpt: applies to new buildings and structures, additions greater than 10 m2, and landscaping (with some exceptions)
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Esquimalt does not permit new development within 20 m of the high-water mark of the Gorge Waterway, or within 10 m of the high-water mark of the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
facts.excerpt: new development is not permitted within 20 metres of the high water mark of the Gorge Waterway, and within 10 m of the high water mark of the Strait
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); an older DPA version cited 7.5 m, so confirm the current figure

facts.text: Esquimalt's DPA 1 guidelines ask designers to avoid disturbing or compacting natural soil, to frame public views rather than block them, and to meet the Canadian Landscape Standards.
facts.sourceTitle: DPA 1 - Natural Environment (Township of Esquimalt, posted 2026-01)
facts.excerpt: avoid disturbing, compacting and removing areas of natural soil
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Esquimalt's Pesticide Use Reduction Bylaw No. 2686 bans non-essential pesticide use on residential properties. It applies to landscape professionals and lawn care companies as well as residents.
facts.sourceTitle: Important Notice to Home Owners, Tenants, Gardeners (Esquimalt pesticide bylaw info sheet)
facts.excerpt: applies to all Esquimalt property owners and residents as well as landscape professionals and lawn care companies
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); sources date from 2008-09, so confirm current text

facts.text: Under Esquimalt's Boulevard Maintenance Bylaw No. 2860, changing a boulevard needs a Boulevard Alteration Permit, and noxious or invasive plants are not allowed on it.
facts.sourceTitle: Boulevard Maintenance Bylaw No. 2860, consolidated July 2019 (Township of Esquimalt)
facts.excerpt: an owner may apply for a Boulevard Alteration Permit
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Esquimalt holds some of the harbour's last Garry oak habitat, including the 2.4-acre Matson Conservation Area. Gardens nearby suit native, invasive-free planting.
facts.note: secondary source; from search snippet; land-trust page

facts.text: Regional (CRD, not municipal): from May 1 to September 30, lawns on the regional water supply may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday). The day limits apply only to lawns.
facts.excerpt: The watering schedule days only apply to lawns!
